bull_bear.body:
- Global leader in Ringback Tones with a 25-year operating history across 2G/3G/4G/5G/AI technology cycles
- Operator relationships averaging over a decade across 67 operators, giving deployment speed and distribution reach the company describes as very difficult to replicate from scratch
- Telco-integrated distribution model for Buzzmo gives access to enterprise (BFSI) deployments that flow through operator channels, a path most standalone CPaaS providers lack
- ONMO streaming patents, including AI-driven streaming and 'snackable moments' gaming, underpinning the Virtual Console/Smart Console product
- Accumulated consumer and telco insights (from two decades of Ringback Tones/Video/Contest services) that funded the strategic pivot into gaming in 2021
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on telecom operator partners — Revenue is earned through revenue-sharing arrangements with telco partners across markets; while this partner network is a competitive strength, it also exposes the business to unilateral commercial changes by partners that affect revenue economics and deployment timelines.
- Structural decline of legacy entertainment services — OTT calling and music streaming are reducing the relevance of Ringback Tones in developed markets, with consumer preferences shifting to on-demand, self-directed content; content licensing arrangements also remain subject to unilateral partner changes that can affect margins, requiring careful commercial/product discipline to manage the transition.
- Geopolitical, regulatory and macroeconomic exposure across a large operating footprint — Operations across 69 countries carry regulatory, technological, operational and macroeconomic risks; an unsettled geopolitical environment and ongoing conflicts create uncertainty around inflation, supply-chain disruption and commodity cost pressures.
- Currency volatility across operating countries — Currency volatility across the Company's 69 operating countries adds further unpredictability to earnings; the Company carries material net foreign-currency denominated monetary assets/liabilities (USD, EUR and other currencies) and uses forward contracts to hedge part of this exposure.
- Intense competition for consumer attention / willingness-to-pay erosion — The most fundamental threat in digital lifestyle services is the consumer's attention span - gaming and entertainment platforms compete with social media, short-form video, OTT and messaging apps for a fixed daily time budget; free-to-access models erode willingness to pay even as production costs rise.
- Rising cloud-gaming input costs — Rising GPU and memory-chip costs, driven by demand for AI infrastructure, are creating potential supply constraints specific to the cloud/console gaming business (Virtual Console / Smart Console).
- Competitive intensity in enterprise communications (Buzzmo) — Enterprise communication is a mature industry with entrenched incumbents, large traffic aggregators and CPaaS platforms competing aggressively on price and scale; protecting share against well-capitalised competitors is described as a sustained effort.
- Tightening AI, data-privacy and digital-payments regulation — Global frameworks governing AI, data privacy, enterprise messaging and digital payments are tightening, and enforcement actions in key markets could disrupt monetisation or delay deployments; billing transparency around subscription confirmations/auto-renewals remains a focus given its impact on consumer trust and brand equity.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: OnMobile Global Limited is a public limited company that provides mobile entertainment and digital lifestyle services to telecom operators, direct consumers, business users and enterprises across 41 countries via revenue-sharing arrangements with telco partners, offering Ringback Tones, a Digital Content Store, Infotainment (video, news, sports, kids content) and gaming. It has diversified into casual/social mobile gaming and cloud-streamed console gaming (ONMO, Challenges Arena, ONMO+ Smart Console) and into AI-powered enterprise communications/CPaaS (Buzzmo) targeting telcos and BFSI customers in Africa and Asia.

outlook.body:
- Expand the gaming business beyond mobile into the console market via the ONMO+ Smart Console, an affordable console-quality cloud gaming solution
- Open new commercial/distribution channels beyond traditional telecom partnerships for Smart Console - e-commerce platforms, retail chains, broadband providers, TV and cable operators
- Use India and Spain as initial Smart Console markets to gather consumer-behaviour and ARPU insights ahead of broader expansion into the Middle East, Asia, Africa and Americas
- Broaden B2B partnerships to introduce Smart Console to new markets and customer segments
- Strengthen gaming marketing through AI-driven forecasting and planning, and expand into new channels and formats
- Expand Buzzmo's presence in Africa, where mobile penetration, financial inclusion and enterprise demand are converging into a single commercial opportunity
- Diversify OnMobile's revenue base by growing gaming and enterprise communications (Buzzmo) alongside the legacy entertainment business
- Maintain prudent capital allocation, directing investment toward technology, product capabilities and infrastructure that support long-term scalability while preserving financial discipline
- Use leasing arrangements for gaming servers and Smart Console controllers (the two largest variable costs of customer growth) to reduce future capital requirements while scaling
- Restore historical collection cycles / DSO to prior levels as a management priority
- Continue deepening investment in automation, AI-driven monitoring and intelligent engineering tools (OARM, AIOps, MLOps) to drive operational and executional efficiency
- Expand the premium gaming catalogue on ONMO and enhance player engagement through differentiated gaming experiences
- Stabilise the video and editorial businesses through newly implemented contracts while contributing new revenue streams
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: OnMobile's expansion is platform/product-led rather than physical-asset-led. FY26 saw the commercial launch of the ONMO+ Smart Console, the culmination of six years of investment in gaming architecture, cloud infrastructure, subscriber management/billing, and streaming/content-delivery technology; during the year the team completed final commercialisation components including AAA cloud-streaming technology integration, optimised server architecture on AMD gaming GPUs, and a multi-device pro controller. Initial rollout covers India and (before year-end) Spain via retail distribution, with the company preparing broader expansion of the Smart Console across the Middle East, Asia, Africa and the Americas, and into new non-telecom distribution channels (e-commerce platforms, retail chains, broadband providers, TV/cable operators). The Gaming & Entertainment Platform (TGEP) expanded its operator footprint by signing Robi in Bangladesh during FY26 and has three additional operator opportunities in advanced stages of closure for FY27. The Tones business is developing a next-generation cloud-native CRBT platform for greater scalability and carrier-grade performance, with first production deployment scheduled for Q2 FY27, and expanded footprint via a brownfield deployment with Claro Peru and a greenfield deployment with Safaricom in Ethiopia. No physical plant, manufacturing capacity or site-based capex is disclosed; the company operates one national office (Bengaluru) and ten overseas branch offices, consistent with an asset-light services/platform model.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global gaming market (~USD 242 billion, expected to reach USD 400 billion) is split nearly evenly between mobile gaming and console & PC gaming; OnMobile's Smart Console lets it address the entire market rather than mobile gaming alone
- Global cloud gaming market projected to reach USD 31.37 billion by 2030 at a 46.8% CAGR (Research and Markets), underpinning the Virtual/Smart Console opportunity
- Global CPaaS market valued at USD 23.19 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 215.36 billion by 2034 at a 28.10% CAGR, as enterprise communication shifts from one-way SMS to AI-powered omnichannel engagement - driving the Buzzmo opportunity
- Global Ringback Tones market valued at USD 4.84 billion in 2024, projected to reach USD 6.67 billion by 2030 at a 4.2% CAGR
- Global MVAS market grew to USD 1.06 trillion in 2025, projected to reach USD 1.89 trillion by 2029 at a 15.4% CAGR, supporting growth in editorial/news subscriptions (Kiosko) and video subscriptions (market expected to reach USD 237.4 billion by 2030)
- Supportive macro conditions across Africa, Asia and Latin America - rising smartphone penetration, expanding financial inclusion and accelerating 5G rollouts - are broadening the addressable base for OnMobile's portfolio
- First-time adoption markets, particularly in Africa (including Ethiopia), remain a genuine growth frontier for both entertainment and gaming as smartphone penetration rises and operator distribution deepens
- India, with more than 500 million gamers and rising middle-class discretionary spending, is a compelling market for gaming and digital entertainment
- Structural threat: consumer attention span is the fundamental constraint, with gaming platforms competing against social media, short-form video, OTT and messaging apps for a fixed daily time budget; free-to-access models erode willingness to pay even as production costs rise
- Threat: rising GPU and memory-chip costs, driven by AI-infrastructure demand, create potential supply constraints specific to cloud gaming
- Threat: network limitations in Tier 2 cities and rural emerging markets, and tightening data-privacy regulation, constrain personalisation across the company's markets
- Legacy Ringback Tones and video face structural headwinds from OTT calling and music streaming eroding relevance in developed markets, requiring careful commercial/product discipline to manage the transition
- Enterprise communications is a mature, competitive industry with entrenched incumbents and large CPaaS platforms competing on price and scale; OnMobile differentiates via its AI layer, telco-integrated delivery and emerging-market focus
- The Gaming & Entertainment Platform (TGEP) has three additional operator deployment opportunities in advanced stages of closure, positioning it to expand its operator footprint in FY27
- Buzzmo secured a multi-year contract with Vodafone Qatar to power enterprise communication and customer engagement, strengthening its presence in the Middle East telecom segment
- Buzzmo enables over 1,000 enterprise clients through a decade-long partnership with a leading Middle East operator
- TGEP expanded its operator footprint during the year by signing with Robi in Bangladesh
- Tones expanded within the America Movil group via a brownfield deployment with Claro Peru (adding an existing subscriber base of approximately 90,000 users), and via a greenfield deployment with Safaricom in Ethiopia that grew to over 750,000 subscribers within eight months of launch
- The Emocion contract with Telefonica Spain (originally set to expire in July 2026) was transitioned via addendum into a yearly auto-renewal arrangement, strengthening continuity and visibility for the infotainment business

deepdive.thesis: OnMobile is a 25-year-old diversified digital lifestyle platform for telecom operators, spanning mobile/console gaming, AI-powered enterprise communications, and mobile entertainment (Ringback Tones, video, infotainment), and is the global leader in Ringback Tones.

open.item: First production deployment of the next-generation cloud-native CRBT platform is scheduled for Q2 FY27.
The Gaming & Entertainment Platform (TGEP) has three additional operator deployment opportunities in advanced stages of closure, expanding its footprint in FY27.
Marketing expense as a percentage of gaming subscription revenue (53% in FY26) expected to fall below 50% during FY27 and progressively move toward the 40-45% range.
Entertainment & Communication business expected to return to positive single-digit revenue growth together with continued progress toward product margins of approximately 25%.
Multiple commercial wins secured by Buzzmo during FY26 are expected to begin contributing additional revenue in FY27.
Management's focus for FY27 is to grow gaming revenues by approximately 50%.
TGEP has three additional operator deployment opportunities in advanced stages of closure, positioning it to further expand its operator footprint in FY27.
Marketing expense as a percentage of gaming subscription revenue targeted to progressively move toward the 40-45% range over the medium term.
Long-term objective of achieving gaming product margins of approximately 25% (11% reached by Q4 FY26).
OnMobile expects to deploy the Smart Console platform in Spain via retail distribution before year-end.
OnMobile is looking to expand Buzzmo's presence in Africa, where converging mobile penetration, financial inclusion and enterprise demand create favourable growth conditions.
Restoring historical collection cycles (DSO rose from 107 to 131 days in FY26, using ~INR 350 million additional working capital) remains a management priority.

Following FY26's commercial launch, OnMobile plans to deploy the Smart Console in Spain via retail distribution before year-end, and to prepare for broader expansion across the Middle East, Asia, Africa and the Americas.
